mainTopic: Blood above and below the red line, the placements that permit and make פיגול, and the status of a חטאת's last three placements.
overview: The amud opens by testing the claim that no essential blood is ever placed half above and half below the red line on the same מזבח. The גמרא tries to read טהרו as 'the middle' of the מזבח, but רבא בר שילא says it means the uncovered top. The שירים don't break the rule, because they are not essential, and the inner offerings use two different altars. Next, a ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב teaches that the minimum placements that permit an offering are also the ones that make it פיגול: two for a חטאת according to בית שמאי, and one according to בית הלל. רבא explains why this case isn't listed among בית שמאי's leniencies: the question was first asked about permitting the meat, where בית שמאי are the strict side. רבי יוחנן and רב פפא then teach that the last three placements of a חטאת are partly like the first placement and partly like the שירים. רב פפא tries to prove the laundering rule from a משנה, the גמרא challenges his inference, and it ties the משנה to רבי נחמיה. When asked whether רבי נחמיה also requires laundering, the גמרא answers 'yes', and the proof comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Does 'on its טהרו' mean the middle of the altar?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the word טהרו means the middle of the מזבח. If so, the seven יום כפורים sprinklings would land partly above and partly below the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: What, is it not talking about the middle of the altar? People say 'clear noon of the day', meaning the middle of the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to find a case that breaks the earlier claim. It suggests that the פסוק's word טהרו means the middle of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rests on everyday speech. The word for noon (טיהרא) shares a root with טהרו, and noon is the middle of the day. If the sprinkling is done at the middle of the מזבח, some blood must fall above the middle and some below, so here would be blood placed half above and half below.

keyTerms.meaning: its half, its middle
noon, the middle of the day
altar
as people say (proof from everyday language)

phrases.english: What, is it not on the middle of the altar?
phrases.notes: This is about the word טהרו from the יום כפורים service, where the כהן גדול sprinkles 'on the טהרו of the מזבח' seven times.

phrases.english: As people say:
"Clear noon of the day"?
phrases.notes: The point is that noon is the middle of the day, so this root would mean 'middle'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the search, from the previous section, for a case where blood is placed half above and half below.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that no blood is ever placed half above and half below the red line.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If טהרו means the middle of the מזבח, seven sprinklings there would land both above and below the middle.

steps.title: רבא בר שילא: טהרו means the uncovered top
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר שילא rejects that reading. He says טהרו means the uncovered top of the מזבח and proves it from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר שילא said: No, it means on its uncovered part, as it is written: 'like the very clear sky.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר שילא pushes back the attempted proof by giving the word טהרו a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the root as 'clear' or 'uncovered', like a clear sky, and not as 'middle'. So the sprinkling is on the top of the מזבח once it has been cleared off. Nothing lands half above and half below, and the earlier claim still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: its uncovered, revealed part
for clearness, clear

phrases.english: Rava bar Sheila said:
No, on its uncovered part;
As it is written: "And like the very sky for clearness."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא בַּר שֵׁילָא: לָא, אַגִּילּוּיֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading proposed in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from טהרו completely.

steps.title: What about the leftover blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the leftover blood (שירים) of a חטאת as a case of blood placed both above and below.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the leftover blood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to the claim. A חטאת gets blood on the upper part of the מזבח, and its leftover blood is poured at the base below.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main placements of a חטאת are above the red line, but the שירים go to the base. So one offering seems to have blood both above and below.

keyTerms.meaning: the leftover blood, poured at the base of the מזבח
but there is! (opens a challenge)

phrases.english: But there is the leftover blood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the טהרו proof fails, the גמרא tries a new case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that no blood is ever placed half above and half below.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חטאת has its main blood above and its שירים below.

steps.title: Leftover blood does not hold up the כפרה
steps.stepSummary: The שירים are not essential, so they do not count against the claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leftover blood does not hold back atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the leftover blood is not needed for the offering to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim was only about blood that is essential for כפרה. The שירים are a מצוה, but skipping them does not ruin the כפרה, so they do not break the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: they hold back, they are essential
atonement

phrases.english: The leftover blood does not hold back atonement.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule to essential blood.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any blood placed below would break the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only blood that is essential for כפרה counts, and שירים are not essential.

steps.title: What about the leftover blood of the inner offerings?
steps.stepSummary: Some hold that the שירים of the inner חטאות are essential, so the challenge comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the leftover blood of the inner offerings, and there is someone who says that it is essential!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer with a case where the leftover blood might be essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood of the inner חטאות is sprinkled on the מזבח הפנימי, and their leftover blood is poured at the base of the outer מזבח. One opinion holds that these שירים are essential, so here would be essential blood both above and below.

keyTerms.meaning: the leftover blood of the inner offerings (offerings whose main blood is sprinkled inside the היכל)
there is someone who says

phrases.english: But there is the leftover blood of the inner offerings,
For there is someone who says they are essential!

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that שירים are not essential.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to one view, the inner שירים are essential and are placed below.

steps.title: The claim is about one altar only
steps.stepSummary: The rule only says that blood is never split above and below on the same מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: We were speaking about one place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that its claim was only about a single מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the inner offerings, the sprinkling is on the inner מזבח and the שירים go on the outer one. These are two different altars, so it is not a case of half above and half below on one מזבח, and the rule holds.

keyTerms.meaning: in one place, on one מזבח
we were saying

steps.whatToRemember: No essential blood is ever placed half above and half below on the same מזבח. Leftover blood is not essential, and the inner offerings use two separate altars.

phrases.english: We were speaking about one place.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule covers blood placed on any altar.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only speaks about a single מזבח.

steps.title: For בית שמאי, the minimum placements both permit and make פיגול
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: for בית שמאי, two placements of a חטאת, or one of any other offering, make the offering permitted and can also make it פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says that בית שמאי say: the two placements of a חטאת, and the one placement of all other offerings, make the offering permitted and make it פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section begins. The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the opinion of בית שמאי from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, בית שמאי say a חטאת needs two placements to work, while other offerings need one. The ברייתא adds that these minimum placements count both ways. They make the meat permitted, and if the כהן had a wrong-time intention while doing them, they make the offering פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: placements of blood on the מזבח
sin offering
they make the offering permitted
they make the offering פיגול (forbidden because of a wrong-time intention)
the school of שמאי

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the rule that whatever placement makes an offering permitted is also the placement where a wrong intention can make it פיגול.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר,
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says,
Beit Shammai say:
The two placements of a sin offering,
And the one placement of all other offerings,
Make the offering permitted and make it piggul.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section about בית שמאי's opinion in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For בית שמאי, the minimum placements (two for a חטאת, one for other offerings) both permit the offering and can make it פיגול.

steps.title: בית הלל: One Placement Is Enough for Every Offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with בית הלל: one placement, for a חטאת and for every other offering, makes the קרבן permitted and can make it פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: one placement in a חטאת, and one placement in all other offerings, makes the offering permitted to eat and can also make it פיגול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא from the last step by giving בית הלל's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי said a חטאת needs two placements. בית הלל say one is enough for a חטאת, just like for any other קרבן. Whatever placement makes the offering permitted is also the placement where a wrong intention makes it פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of הלל, who argue with בית שמאי
Makes permitted, so the meat may be eaten
Makes the offering פיגול through a wrong intention about time

steps.whatToRemember: For בית הלל, one placement does everything: it permits the meat, and a wrong intention during it creates פיגול.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel say:
One placement in a sin offering
and one placement in all the other offerings
permits the offering and can make it piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא of step 7 by giving the other side of the מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For בית הלל, a single placement, for a חטאת or any other offering, permits the offering and can make it פיגול.

steps.title: Why Isn't This Listed Among בית שמאי's Leniencies?
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא asks that if so, this case should appear in the list of cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא objects: if so, this should be taught together with the cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא challenges the ברייתא. In his view, here בית הלל come out stricter about פיגול, so the case should be in the famous list of such unusual cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known list of the rare cases where בית שמאי are the lenient side. Under בית הלל, one placement with a wrong intention already makes a חטאת פיגול, while בית שמאי need two. That makes בית הלל stricter, so why isn't this case on the list?

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it, raises a strong challenge
Let it be taught, it should have been listed

keyTerms.term: קוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
keyTerms.meaning: The list of cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict

phrases.english: Rav Oshaya objects to this:
If so, let it be taught
together with the leniencies of Beit Shammai
phrases.notes: He means the special list of these unusual cases, found in מסכת עדיות.

phrases.english: and the stringencies of Beit Hillel!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא: אִם כֵּן, לִיתְנְיַיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא of steps 7 and 8 from the way the tradition records בית שמאי's leniencies.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's report of the מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On פיגול, בית הלל come out stricter than בית שמאי. Such cases are rare and were collected in a list, so this one should have been included.

steps.title: The Question Was About Permitting the Meat
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the question was first asked about permitting the meat, and on that side בית שמאי are the strict ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: when this question was asked, it was asked about permitting, so בית שמאי turn out to be the strict side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מחלוקת started from the question of when the meat of a חטאת becomes permitted. On that point בית שמאי, who need two placements, are stricter than בית הלל, who need only one. Since the case was framed that way, it does not belong in the list of בית שמאי's leniencies.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked
About permitting, here permitting the meat to be eaten
On the strict side

steps.whatToRemember: The same מחלוקת can look lenient or strict depending on which side you ask about. Asked about permitting the meat, בית שמאי are strict.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
When it was asked, it was asked about permitting the meat;
so Beit Shammai are the ones who are stringent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אושעיא's קשיא from step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: it shows which side of the מחלוקת the original question was about.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since בית הלל are stricter about פיגול, the case should be counted among בית שמאי's leniencies.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question was about permitting the meat, where בית שמאי are stricter, so the case does not belong on that list.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: Three Laws About the Remaining Placements of a חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the three remaining placements of a חטאת cannot be done at night, can be done after the owner dies, and make a person liable if offered outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the three placements of the חטאות are not done at night, they are done after the owner's death, and one who offers them up outside the מקדש is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a statement of רבי יוחנן about the extra placements of a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית הלל, only the first placement is essential, so one might think the other three placements have no real status. רבי יוחנן teaches that they still have real laws. Like regular blood service they cannot be done at night, and offering them outside the מקדש still makes a person liable. Yet unlike the first placement, they may be done even after the owner has died.

keyTerms.meaning: Placements of blood on the מזבח
After the death of the owner of the קרבן
One who offers up a קרבן outside the מקדש
Liable, deserving punishment

steps.confusionAlert: The "three placements" are not the main one. They are the three extra placements after the first one, which already brought atonement.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a non-essential part of the service is still a real part of the עבודה, with its own laws.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
The three placements of the sin offerings
phrases.notes: He means the three that come after the first placement, out of the four placements of a חטאת.

phrases.english: may not be performed at night,
and may be performed after the owner's death,
and one who offers any of them outside is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: שָׁלֹשׁ מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁבַּחַטָּאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on בית הלל's view in step 8 that only one placement is essential, and sets out the laws of the remaining three.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three non-essential placements of a חטאת cannot be done at night, can be done after the owner dies, and offering them outside the מקדש makes a person liable.

steps.title: The last three placements are partly like the beginning and partly like the end
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא states a general principle: the last three placements of a חטאת are sometimes treated like the first placement and sometimes like the leftover blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: In some ways they are like the beginning, and in some ways they are like the end.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a general rule about the three remaining placements of a חטאת. He is setting up two lists that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן already showed that these placements share some rules with the first placement. רב פפא now says they are a mixed case. Sometimes they act like the main service at the start, and sometimes like the שירים at the end.

keyTerms.meaning: Like its beginning, meaning treated like the first placement
Like its end, meaning treated like the leftover blood

phrases.english: Rav Pappa says:
There are some of them like its beginning
phrases.notes: "Them" means the last three placements of the חטאת's blood from the previous step.

phrases.english: and there are some of them like its end;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: יֵשׁ מֵהֶן כִּתְחִלָּתוֹ וְיֵשׁ מֵהֶן כְּסוֹפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יוחנן's teaching and turns it into a full system of 'beginning' versus 'end' rules.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The last three placements of a חטאת have a mixed status: partly like the first placement, partly like the שירים.

steps.title: The rules where the last three placements are like the first
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא lists eight rules where the last three placements are treated like the first placement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Offering outside, night, a non-כהן, service vessels, the corner of the altar, the finger, laundering, and the leftover blood: in all these they are like the beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא lists the rules where the last three placements are treated just like the first, main placement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Offering them outside makes a person liable. They cannot be done at night or by a non-כהן. The blood must be in a כלי שרת and placed with the finger on the קרן. Blood from them that splashes on a garment needs כיבוס. The שירים still have to be poured out after them.

keyTerms.meaning: Being a non-כהן, which disqualifies a person from the service
Sacred service vessels of the בית המקדש
Corner of the altar, where the blood is placed
Laundering a garment that חטאת blood splashed onto
The leftover blood, poured on the base of the altar

phrases.english: Outside, and night, a non-priest,
and service vessels, corner, and finger,
laundering, and the remainder – like their beginning;
phrases.notes: "Remainder" means that even after these three placements, the leftover blood must still be poured out, just as after the first.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוּץ, וְלַיְלָה, זָרוּת, וּכְלֵי שָׁרֵת, קֶרֶן, וְאֶצְבַּע, כִּיבּוּס, וְשִׁירַיִם – כִּתְחִלָּתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the 'like the beginning' half of רב פפא's general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the rules of outside, night, a non-כהן, service vessels, the corner, the finger, laundering, and the שירים, the last three placements are like the first.

steps.title: The rules where the last three placements are like the leftover blood
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא lists four rules where the last three placements are treated like the שירים at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they may be done after the owner dies, they do not make the meat permitted, they do not make it פיגול, and blood brought inside does not disqualify: in these they are like the end.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his rule by listing where the last three placements are treated like the leftover blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first placement already did the main job: it made the meat permitted. So the later placements do not permit, and wrong intent during them cannot make the offering פיגול. They may also be done after the owner dies. If their blood is brought into the היכל, the offering is not disqualified.

keyTerms.meaning: After the death of the owner of the קרבן
Permits, meaning makes the meat allowed to eat
Makes the offering פיגול through wrong intent about time
Inside, meaning into the היכל

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the later placements are optional. They must still be done. They just do not have the power of the first placement to permit the meat or create פיגול.

phrases.english: But they may be done after death,
phrases.notes: He means after the death of the person who brought the קרבן.

phrases.english: they do not permit, and they do not make it piggul,
and they do not [disqualify by] entering inside – like their end.
phrases.notes: If this blood is carried into the היכל, the חטאת isn't ruined, unlike blood from the first placement.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבָאוֹת לְאַחַר מִיתָה, לָא שָׁרְיָא, וְלָא מְפַגְּלָא, וְלָא עָיְילָא לְגַוַּאי – כְּסוֹפָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the 'like the end' half of רב פפא's general rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This matches בית הלל's view from step 8: only one placement permits the meat and can make it פיגול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The last three placements may be done after the owner's death, do not permit the meat, do not make it פיגול, and do not disqualify the offering by entering the היכל.

steps.title: Proof that laundering applies to the last three placements
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא proves from a משנה that blood still waiting to go on the corner requires laundering, so the last three placements need כיבוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: How do I know this? From a משנה: blood that sprayed from the animal's neck onto a garment does not need laundering. Blood that sprayed from the corner or the base does not need laundering. This implies that blood still fit for the corner does need laundering.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a source for one item on his list: that blood from the last three placements requires כיבוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts blood from the neck, because it was never in a vessel. It also exempts blood from the קרן or יסוד, because it was already used. That implies blood that is still fit for the קרן does need laundering. Blood for the last three placements is still fit for the קרן, so it needs כיבוס.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say it? This opens a proof
Sprayed or splashed
The neck of the animal, where it is slaughtered
The base of the altar
Blood that is still fit to be placed on the corner

steps.whatToRemember: The last three placements are a mixed case. For service rules like night, a non-כהן, the vessel, the finger, the corner and laundering, they count like the first placement. For permitting, פיגול, the owner's death, and entering inside, they count like the leftover blood. רב פפא's proof for the laundering rule, from the משנה's 'fit for the corner' inference, is challenged in the next steps. The גמרא ends up tying it to רבי נחמיה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: From where do I say it?
phrases.notes: "It" is the laundering rule from his first list.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
If it sprayed from the neck onto the garment –
it does not require laundering.
From the corner or from the base –
it does not require laundering.
This implies: from blood fit for the corner –
phrases.notes: This is רב פפא's own inference. The last three placements' blood hasn't gone on the corner yet, so it is still "fit for the corner."

phrases.english: it requires laundering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the laundering item from step 13 with a source in a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That blood of the last three placements of a חטאת requires כיבוס, like the first placement.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about blood splashing onto a garment: from the neck or from the קרן and יסוד it is exempt, which implies that blood still fit for the קרן requires laundering.

steps.title: By the same logic, the leftover blood would need laundering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's style of inference. The same reading would mean that blood fit for the יסוד (the שירים) needs כיבוס, but the פסוק ״אשר יזה״ excludes blood that was already sprinkled.
steps.simpleTranslation: But by your reasoning: blood from the base does not need laundering, so blood that is still fit for the base does need laundering?! Yet the verse says 'that will be sprinkled', which excludes this blood that was already sprinkled!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב פפא's proof from Step 15 by showing that the same kind of reading leads to a result that goes against a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא drew an inference from what the משנה left out. The גמרא says that if you read it that way, you must also infer that the שירים still waiting for the יסוד need כיבוס. But the word ״יזה״ is in the future tense, so it only covers blood that has not yet been sprinkled. The שירים come after the sprinkling is done, so they should be exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning (turning a person's own logic against him)
The base of the מזבח, where the leftover blood is poured
Laundering a garment that חטאת blood splashed on
Was already sprinkled
To exclude this case

phrases.aramaic: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, מִן הַיְסוֹד אֵינוֹ טָעוּן כִּיבּוּס –
phrases.english: But according to your reasoning: blood from the base does not require laundering,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is copying the same kind of reading רב פפא used on the משנה in Step 15.

phrases.aramaic: הָא מִן הָרָאוּי לַיְסוֹד טָעוּן כִּיבּוּס?!
phrases.english: so blood that is fit for the base would require laundering?!
phrases.notes: 'Fit for the base' means the leftover blood after the placements, which still has to be poured at the base.

phrases.english: But it is written: 'that will be sprinkled',
which excludes this blood that was already sprinkled!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, מִן הַיְסוֹד אֵינוֹ טָעוּן כִּיבּוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method of inference used in רב פפא's proof in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's inference from the משנה that blood still fit for the corner requires כיבוס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same inference would mean the שירים need כיבוס, but ״אשר יזה״ excludes blood that was already sprinkled. So the method proves too much.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי נחמיה. He holds that offering the שירים outside makes a person liable, so he treats leftover blood as real blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It is רבי נחמיה's. As we learned: רבי נחמיה says, if someone offered the leftover blood outside the Temple, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the reading of the משנה. It explains that the משנה follows רבי נחמיה, who treats the leftover blood as important, real blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נחמיה, the שירים are serious enough that offering them outside brings liability. So it is no problem for him if the שירים also need כיבוס, and the challenge from ״אשר יזה״ only works against the חכמים. That means רב פפא's proof holds according to רבי נחמיה.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
The leftover blood after the required placements
Offered them outside the Temple
Liable

phrases.english: Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Neḥemya's;
as we learned in a Mishnah, Rabbi Neḥemya says:
leftover blood that one offered outside, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16 by assigning the משנה to רבי נחמיה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a specific תנא (רבי נחמיה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה follows everyone, so the inference would clash with ״אשר יזה״.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי נחמיה, who treats שירים as real blood, so the inference stands for him.

steps.title: Maybe רבי נחמיה only meant offering outside, not laundering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי נחמיה's ruling about offering outside also applies to כיבוס. Maybe he only treats שירים like אברים and פדרים, which bring liability outside even though they are not needed for atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say you heard רבי נחמיה rule this way about offering up the blood, just like limbs and fats. But about laundering, did you hear him say it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 17. It asks whether רבי נחמיה's ruling about offering outside really tells us anything about כיבוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability for offering outside does not prove that something counts as real blood. אברים and פדרים are not needed for atonement, yet offering them outside still brings liability. So רבי נחמיה might hold the שירים are like them for offering outside, without saying that they need כיבוס.

keyTerms.meaning: Say that you heard him rule this way (only in this area)
Offering up (here, offering outside the Temple)
Limbs of the animal burned on the מזבח
Fats burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that 'liable for offering outside' means 'counts as real blood for every law'. The גמרא is pointing out that these can be separate.

phrases.english: Say that you heard Rabbi Neḥemya rule this way
regarding offering up,
just as it is with limbs and fats;
phrases.notes: Limbs and fats are not needed for atonement, yet offering them outside still makes a person liable.

phrases.english: but regarding laundering, did you hear him say it?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 17, which stretched רבי נחמיה's ruling to cover כיבוס.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי נחמיה's ruling on offering outside also means שירים need כיבוס.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Liability for offering outside also applies to אברים and פדרים, which are not blood at all. So it does not prove that שירים count as real blood for כיבוס.

steps.title: Yes, רבי נחמיה also requires laundering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that yes, we did hear רבי נחמיה rule this way about כיבוס too. The source is about to be brought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in one word: 'Yes'. It is setting up the next move, where it will bring a source showing that רבי נחמיה also requires כיבוס for שירים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer keeps the defense of רב פפא's proof alive. The proof for the 'Yes' comes at the start of the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes (Aramaic)

phrases.english: Yes;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 18 and leads into a proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Direct confirmation, with a proof to follow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי נחמיה only made the שירים liable when offered outside, like אברים and פדרים.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי נחמיה also requires כיבוס for the שירים.
